title: Where Proto-Indo-European was first spoken
summary: The steppe theory is the most widely accepted and the Anatolian hypothesis is largely abandoned, but where the archaic stage arose, and how some branches spread, is still debated.
why: It is the ancestor of languages from Ireland to India.

notes.problem: Steppe homeland for late PIE is near-consensus; open part is archaic PIE. 'Near the Caucasus' conflated the north-Caucasus steppe proposal with the south-Caucasus Armenian hypothesis.

question: Where was the earliest, archaic stage of Proto-Indo-European spoken: on the steppe or south of the Caucasus?
evidence: Steppe origin dated about 4000–3000 BCE; newer proposals put archaic PIE between the Caucasus and lower Volga about 4400–4000 BCE.
wouldSettle: Ancient genomes and archaeology tracing a single population to the earliest Anatolian and steppe language splits.

theories.name: Pontic–Caspian steppe
theories.idea: All PIE stages arose on the steppe; Lazaridis and Anthony put archaic PIE between Caucasus and lower Volga, 4400–4000 BCE.

theories.name: South of the Caucasus (Armenian)
theories.idea: Archaic PIE was spoken south of the Caucasus before a branch moved onto the steppe.
